## Energy / XLE — 2026-08-28

This is a **continuation oil-down / relative-fade** session, not a fresh Hormuz squeeze and not an 08-25-style crude collapse. Live oil is still red, but the move is modest on WTI. The 08-27 miss was magnitude (notable into a flat close) after a non-transmitting green 08-26 print. Do not repeat S1=−2 / notable.

### Channel 2

**1. Shared macro as it hits energy.** Tape is **flat, not risk-on**: ES=F 0.0%, NQ=F −0.19%, Finviz SPX −0.12% / NQ −0.29%. Asia composite −0.15% (Kospi −1.79%); Europe −0.72% (CAC −1.68%, FTSE −0.79%). VIX 14.51 (calm), Fear & Greed 58.2 Greed. DXY 1d −0.02% / Finviz USD +0.04% — **not** a USD-up commodity hit. DFII10 2.34, +0.02 1d — real yields slightly firmer, **secondary vs oil**. Sticky July core PCE 3.3% is **already in** (08-26); News Judge ranks **Warsh Jackson Hole (~10:00 ET today)** as the residual two-sided policy binary, not an energy spine. NVDA/software leadership is XLK/NQ, not XLE. For this cyclical, flat futures + leftover tech leadership is **not** a bid. **S0 muted at 0.**

**2. Spine (S1).** Count the oil shock **once**. Re-verified live.
- **Crude down, not collapse:** CL=F −0.8%, BZ=F −1.91%, Finviz WTI $83.01 (−0.63%). Live WTI ~$83.0–83.25, Brent ~$88.3–88.5. Same sign as Channel 1 — 08-11 passes. Brent’s −1.9% is the firmer leg; WTI is sub-1%. This is **not** 08-25’s −3% collapse and **not** enough to restore S1=−2 under the 08-27 falsifier unless inventory also shocks live (it does not).
- **EIA already out (08-26, week ending 8/21):** crude **+0.1 Mb to 428.9 Mb** (barely a build); gasoline **−2.5 Mb**; distillate **−2.23 Mb**. Next print **Sep 2**. Do **not** date this as today’s catalyst. Not a live bearish inventory shock; products actually drew.
- **OPEC+ adding barrels (carried):** Aug **+188 kb/d**; Sep another ~188 kb/d to finish the 2023 voluntary-cut rollback, then pause. Not a cut.
- **Demand destruction (official, carried):** IEA Aug OMR 2026 demand **−1.6 mb/d**; OPEC still **+0.6 mb/d**. Two-sided official book; do not triple-count with the oil print.
- **Geo premium not transmitting:** Hormuz/Iran copy is still in the tape (08-24 tanker blacklist, mid-Aug seizures), but **oil is falling**. Score fade/non-confirmation — **do not** also score Crude oil price surge.
- **Cracks still extreme** (3-2-1 ~$67–71; diesel crack still ~$93–99) — **refiner offset only**; dampen for whole XLE. Do not let VLO/MPC carry the ETF while crude is soft.
- **Nat gas ~$2.92 (+0.10%)** — no surge; N/A for oil-weighted XLE.

Net S1 = **−1**. Not −2: 08-27 forbids recycling the multi-day stack; WTI is only ~−0.6/−0.8%; EIA/PCE are stale; product draws + cracks cushion. Not 0: live oil sign is still down and OPEC+ is still adding.

**3. Breadth.** 1d/3d/1w relative all red (−0.88% / −2.30% / −3.40%). 08-27 internals: XOM −1.11%, COP −0.83%, CVX modestly red with the ETF — large-caps participating in the fade, not mega-name carry. Leadership stalling. **S2 = −1.**

**4. Flows / positioning.** Independent of the tape: XLE ~**−$698M 5d / −$1.14B 1m**; 08-25 single-day **−$458M**; energy ETFs ~$4B out over ~65 days. Crowded long after the Hormuz run is still unwinding. Rotation **out of energy**. **S3 = −1** (flows, not a second copy of S2). 08-27: do not let S2+S3 plus S1=−2 print notable — S1 is already capped at −1.

**5. Catalysts.** No fresh XLE-wide earnings. **Warsh JH today** is two-sided (hawkish confirmation could firm USD/yields and press oil; a no-drama speech is a fade). PCE and EIA are **not** today’s 8:30. Hormuz headlines are **not** an oil-up catalyst at the open.

### Scoring logic

S0 = **0**: flat ES, slightly soft NQ/Europe, calm VIX. Not −1 (no liquidation). Not +1 (would fight the oil spine; NVDA is not an XLE holding).

S1 = **−1**: live oil down once + carried OPEC+ add / IEA demand, minus damped cracks and a two-sided EIA. 08-27 cap applied.

S2/S3/S4 all confirm **relative fade**. S4 is confirmation only: 1d rel **−0.88%** is decisive, not a sub-0.5% bounce. **No leading-vs-tape divergence** — factors and tape agree lower. Trust factors.

Magnitude: **mild, not notable.** Oil is not collapsing; last session already failed to deliver notable; Energy mag hit-rate **0.2**; Warsh is two-sided; 08-27 explicitly caps mag at mild/flat after the oil-down stack unless CL/BZ ~−1% **and** transmitting. Brent −1.91% is the only argument for notable; WTI −0.63/−0.8% plus S4 already in the price argues **mild**. Multiplier **0.9**. Confidence **0.52** (keep direction, shrink conviction per the Energy experiment).

Regime **mixed**: SPX beta is flat; the Energy call is the oil spine, not SPX.

Self-audit: lens = XLE/oil, not SPX; band reconciled to mild; no same-shock triple-count of oil; refiners not allowed to drive the ETF; no single-ticker call; EIA/PCE not dated as live; narrative and components both **down/mild**.

## 0. Facts

XLE opened **62.35**, closed **62.68**, **+0.626%**. SPY **−0.227%**. Relative **+0.853%**. Path: modest range (high ~62.74 / low ~62.12) — no collapse, no melt-up. Direction **up**, magnitude **mild**.

Morning call: **down / mild**, total **−6.3**, S0=0 / S1=S2=S3=S4=−1, conf 0.52. **Direction miss, magnitude hit.**

This is the inverse of 08-27 (dir HIT / mag MISS into a flat −0.22% close). The Energy experiment — “keep direction, shrink confidence after mag misses” — failed on the direction it was designed to protect.

## 1. What drove Energy today

Taxonomy, in order of transmission:

**Crack / refining-margin expansion (HIT, and it transmitted).** Crude did not lead. RBOB gasoline futures closed **+3.12%** while WTI was roughly flat-to-soft. VLO **+1.66%**, PSX **+1.75%** — refiners were the internal leadership. Morning explicitly treated extreme cracks as a *dampen*, not a driver (“do not let VLO/MPC carry the ETF while crude is soft”). They carried enough, with CVX, to flip the ETF.

**Crude oil price move (MISS as a same-day down spine).** Premarket Channel 1 had CL=F **−0.8%** / BZ=F **−1.91%**, Finviz WTI **$83.01 (−0.63%)**. By the cash close that shock had mostly faded: Texas Energy Report **WTI $83.40 (−0.16%)**, **Brent $89.31 (−0.43%)**; Oilprice midday **WTI $83.21 (−0.38%)**, **Brent $89.36 (−0.39%)**. Weekly crude was still down ~4–5%, but **Friday was not a fresh oil-down day**. Scoring S1=−1 off the open print treated a leftover weekly fade as a live transmitter.

**Large-cap leadership inside the sector (HIT, opposite sign from morning).** CVX **+1.04%** (idiosyncratic Venezuela-fields headline plus beta), COP **+0.64%**, XOM only **+0.17%**. Majors were green, not repeating 08-27’s XOM −1.11% / COP −0.83% fade. S2=−1 was yesterday’s internals.

**Warsh Jackson Hole as shared macro, not energy spine.** Speech was hawkish on inflation (“we have work to do”) with no oil call. SPY sold off ~0.23%; 2y yields and hike odds rose. Morning S0=0 was fair as *not an XLE catalyst*, but the inference “flat futures + leftover tech leadership is **not a bid**” missed the relative-rotation case: hawkish Fed + soft crude can still bid XLE vs SPY if cracks hold and the 1w relative −3.40% mean-reverts.

**Geopolitical premium / OPEC+ / EIA / IEA demand (carried, non-transmitting).** No new EIA (next Sep 2). OPEC+ add and IEA −1.6 mb/d demand were already in the weekly oil drop. Hormuz copy still not spiking oil. Baker Hughes oil rigs **−5 to 447** (total 588 unchanged) was a Friday print, mildly constructive for crude, not an XLE-wide shock.

**Nat gas:** ~$2.89 (−0.9%) — N/A for oil-weighted XLE, as morning said.

## 2. Audit of morning S0–S4 (use morning numbers, do not rewrite them)

| Sleeve | Morning | Reality | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S0 0** | ES 0.0%, NQ −0.19%, VIX 14.51, Warsh two-sided, “not a bid” | SPY −0.23% after hawkish Warsh; XLE **up** vs that dip | S0=0 as “not liquidation / not risk-on” was ok. The “not a bid” clause was the miss — energy *was* the relative bid. |
| **S1 −1** | Live oil down once, OPEC+ add, IEA demand; **capped at −1** per 08-27; cracks damped | Oil faded to ~flat; RBOB +3%; refiners led | Cap vs −2 was correct. Residual −1 still overstated a non-transmitting open print. Crack dampen was the wrong sign for *today*. |
| **S2 −1** | 1d/3d/1w rel red; 08-27 XOM/COP participation in fade | CVX/COP/XOM green; refiners stronger; FANG/EOG the laggards | Stale. Prior-day large-cap fade did not persist. |
| **S3 −1** | XLE ~−$698M 5d / −$1.14B 1m; rotation out | Positioning unwind did not dominate a +0.63% / +0.85% rel session | Independent in principle, but it was another copy of the same fade narrative. |
| **S4 −1** | 1d rel −0.88% “decisive” | That was **08-27**. Today rel **+0.85%** | Using yesterday’s relative tape as today’s factor is lookback. |

**08-27 lesson, applied:** Do not restore S1=−2 / notable off the multi-day oil-down stack. **Followed.** Mag stayed mild. **Not applied:** once the stack has already failed to deliver, “keep direction down” is still recycling the same shock. Confidence 0.52 did not save a signed −6.3.

**Hit-grid vs close:** Crude price surge MISS (correct). Crude collapse only PARTIAL at the open and **false by the close**. Crack expansion HIT and was the actual driver — morning scored it HIT then **damped it out of S1**. Sector rotation *out* of energy HIT at the open, **false by the close** (rel +0.85%). OPEC+ increase / IEA demand HIT as background, not Friday news.

## 3. Interactions / double-count / knowable-at-open

**Double-count:** S1 (oil down) + S2 (names fading with oil) + S3 (outflows after Hormuz unwind) + S4 (1d/3d/1w rel red) are **one multi-day oil-down/relative-fade**. Capping S1 at −1 and mag at mild was the intended anti-stack. Summing four −1s into −6.3 **down** still treated one leftover shock as four confirming sleeves.

**Knowable at open — yes:** WTI only ~−0.6/−0.8% (not 08-25 collapse); EIA/PCE stale; cracks still extreme; Warsh two-sided; 08-27 mag miss; 1w rel already −3.40% (mean-reversion risk). Morning wrote all of this.

**Knowable at open — no:** WTI/Brent recovering most of the premarket red; RBOB **+3.12%** on the session; WSJ Chevron/Venezuela fields story; energy catching a relative bid while SPY sold Warsh.

**Partially** is the honest label: the *mild* call was in the information set; the *down* call required the open oil print to keep transmitting, which 08-27 had just falsified.

## 4. Outliers inside the sector

**Leaders (crack / integrated, not E&P):** PSX +1.75%, VLO +1.66%, CVX +1.04% (Venezuela-fields overlay), COP +0.64%.  
**Laggards (upstream):** FANG **−1.43%**, EOG **−0.80%**, OXY ~−0.12%. XOM **+0.17%** — mega-cap did not lead; this was not an XOM squeeze.  
**Mapping:** refiners > integrated > E&P is exactly “crude soft, products tight.” Morning forbade that mapping from driving XLE. On a +0.63% ETF day it was enough, especially with CVX’s stock-specific bid.

Utilities/power (VST −1.95%, NRG −2.88%) sold off — **not XLE**, but useful: Friday’s energy bid was oil-products, not the AI-power complex Warsh name-checked.
